messages.subject: Prediction of unobserved data
parts:
Dear All,

I am just wondering if I undertsand well the way to predict missing values with INLA. Actually I assume that all predicted values are based on the predictive distributions, but I have a question concerning the prediction of random effect for which we have no realization of one level?

Thanks for your help.
Regards,
Marie.

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prediction of unobserved data
parts:
Your question is quite general. Maybe
https://haakonbakka.bitbucket.io/btopic112.html
will help (the title is wrong, it should be "binomial")

Under
https://haakonbakka.bitbucket.io/btopic112.html#alternative-way-building-up-the-samples-model-component-by-model-component
you see how to build up a posterior sample through the linear predictor.

If you have no realisation for one level, you will need to sample "a new level" in the random effect. How this is done depends on your random effect. For this iid effect you would sample from a mean zero iid effect with the same standard deviation as the other levels (which you find in samples[[nr]]$hyperpar).

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka
